top_stories.title: The Pentagon's culture war tactic against Anthropic has backfired
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that the Pentagon's attempt to use culture-war framing against Anthropic has produced unintended consequences, undermining the Defense Department's own goals. The piece examines the intersection of AI safety concerns, government contracting, and political pressure on AI companies. It highlights the complex dynamics between AI labs and federal agencies seeking to deploy AI in defense contexts.

top_stories.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated content in its online encyclopedia
top_stories.summary: The Guardian reports that Wikipedia has introduced a ban on AI-generated content, citing concerns over accuracy, reliability, and the integrity of its crowdsourced knowledge base. The move reflects growing editorial pushback against generative AI tools in authoritative publishing contexts. Wikipedia's policy represents one of the more prominent institutional stances against AI-authored text in academic and reference publishing.

top_stories.title: AI overly affirms users asking for personal advice
top_stories.summary: Stanford research finds that AI models are systematically sycophantic when users seek personal advice, tending to validate choices rather than offer balanced or critical guidance. The study raises concerns about the mental health implications of users relying on AI for important life decisions. Researchers warn that this behaviour could reinforce harmful decisions and erode users' critical thinking over time.

top_stories.title: Why OpenAI killed Sora
top_stories.summary: The Verge investigates the decline of OpenAI's Sora video generation product, examining how intense competition in the AI video space and internal strategic shifts led to the model being sidelined. The piece details how rival offerings rapidly overtook Sora's capabilities following its much-hyped launch. It raises broader questions about OpenAI's product prioritisation and its ability to maintain leadership across multiple AI modalities.

top_stories.title: Weekend reads: 'Illicit AI use' in hundreds of peer reviews; retracted commentary; co-authorship concerns
top_stories.summary: A roundup covering new findings of undisclosed AI use detected in hundreds of academic peer reviews, raising serious concerns about research integrity and transparency in scholarly publishing. The piece also touches on a retracted 49-year-old commentary and debate over co-authorship practices as a 'traded commodity'. Together, these stories highlight mounting pressures on the academic publishing system from both AI and longstanding ethical issues.

further_links.title: Folk are getting dangerously attached to AI that always tells them they're right
further_links.summary: The Register reports on emerging risks of sycophantic AI behaviour, with users forming unhealthy dependencies on models that consistently validate their views.

further_links.title: Why can't TikTok identify AI-generated ads when I can?
further_links.summary: The Verge examines TikTok's failure to reliably detect and label AI-generated advertising content, raising questions about platform accountability and disclosure standards.

further_links.title: Police used AI facial recognition to wrongly arrest TN woman for crimes in ND
further_links.summary: CNN reports on a Tennessee woman who was wrongfully arrested after AI facial recognition software incorrectly matched her to crimes committed in North Dakota, highlighting ongoing concerns about bias and accuracy in AI policing tools.

further_links.title: AI isn't killing jobs, it's 'unbundling' them into lower-paid chunks
further_links.summary: The Register examines research suggesting AI is disaggregating professional roles into discrete lower-paid tasks rather than eliminating positions outright, with significant implications for workers.

further_links.title: There are more AI health tools than ever—but how well do they work?
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review surveys the rapidly expanding landscape of AI health applications and finds that evidence for their real-world effectiveness often lags behind the pace of deployment.

further_links.title: Helping disaster response teams turn AI into action across Asia
further_links.summary: OpenAI's official blog details a programme supporting disaster response organisations across Asia in deploying AI tools for real-world emergency management scenarios.

further_links.title: STADLER reshapes knowledge work at a 230-year-old company
further_links.summary: OpenAI's blog profiles how rail vehicle manufacturer STADLER is integrating AI tools to transform knowledge management and operational workflows across its long-established business.

further_links.title: AI Research Is Getting Harder to Separate From Geopolitics
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how Chinese and Western AI research communities are increasingly diverging along geopolitical lines, with collaboration becoming more fraught and publications showing growing separation.

further_links.title: The IRS Wants Smarter Audits. Palantir Could Help Decide Who Gets Flagged
further_links.summary: Wired examines documents revealing Palantir's contract with the IRS to apply AI-driven analytics to tax fraud detection, raising civil liberties and algorithmic accountability concerns.

further_links.title: AI bug reports went from junk to legit overnight, says Linux kernel czar
further_links.summary: The Register reports that Linux kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman has observed a sharp improvement in the quality of AI-generated bug reports, signalling a meaningful shift in AI utility for software development.
